kai (AcmeCorp): hi team — since ~2026-03-16 01:17 UTC our integration started returning 401 invalid_api_key for every request. nothing changed on our side, same key in env

kai (AcmeCorp): example curl we run from our server:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: ApiKey sk.prod.abc123def456' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

emma-support: thanks, sorry for the disruption. can you paste any request id/trace-id from the response headers (x-rw-trace-id) or a log snippet? also are you using any org-level security policies? :thinking:

kai (AcmeCorp): reply header shows `x-rw-trace-id: trc_20260316_7f9a` and full response body: `{"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}}`

emma-support: looking up the trace... one sec.

policy-bot: policy-check trc_20260316_7f9a -> denied by policy `api_key_otp_required` (org: acmecorp)

emma-support: ah — our policy engine shows your org has `api_key_otp_required` enabled. that requires an additional header with a one-time code for API key usage from non-interactive clients. did your integration previously include an OTP header?

kai (AcmeCorp): hmm no, our CI server doesn't do OTP. this was working before though — did something change on Redwood side?

oliver-eng: yep this was a targeted security feature rolled out last night for orgs that opt into stricter key policies (enterprise tier). if you enable it the platform rejects plain key usage unless a valid TOTP/OTP is supplied in `X-API-Key-OTP`. we should have notified org admins — looks like acmecorp opted in via the console.

emma-support: two options: 1) update your client to send the OTP header (we support TOTP apps and short-lived OTPs issued via the Console/API), or 2) generate a new org-scoped key that has `otp_required=false` (if your org policy allows creating non-OTP keys) or use a service principal token.

kai (AcmeCorp): how do we generate the OTP from CI? we don't have an interactive TFA device attached to the runner.

oliver-eng: recommended pattern for CI is to create a service credential with OTP disabled (better: a short-lived service token minted by your identity provider) or to use our one-time-API endpoint to mint a session token (requires auth with a backed service account). doc snippet: add header `-H 'X-API-Key-OTP: 123456'` where 123456 is the TOTP code tied to the API key activation flow. I'll paste the internal runbook link in the thread.

emma-support: @kai (AcmeCorp) for a quick unblock we can: a) temporarily toggle `api_key_otp_required` off for a specific application (if your org admin approves) or b) issue a short-lived service token from Support while you set up service credentials. which do you prefer?

kai (AcmeCorp): admin prefers option b. can you issue a temp token and share rotation steps?

emma-support: sure — escalating to security ops. @oliver-eng any audit implications for issuing a support temp token for acmecorp? :lock:

oliver-eng: fine to issue short-lived token, we log issuance and set TTL 1h. advise customer to rotate to proper service principal within the hour. I'll create the token now and DM the value to the org owner. adding product to follow up on notification flow.

emma-support: created support ticket RW-5234 and flagged for postmortem on admin notifications. Kai, I'll DM the token to your org owner address and update the ticket with next steps. sorry again — let us know if anything else fails. :pray:
